final_recommendation: The room converged on a trilateral package: 65-70-75% RVC glide path over three years, quarterly labor audits with 30-day certification and plant-specific tariff suspension for wage-floor violations, and a binding ministerial statement preserving Canada's dairy supply management and Chapter 19 in the ratification instrument. USTR filed the operational protocol with all three governments, and all parties committed ratification support.
minority_objections: Dairy_ag initially demanded 3.25% Class 7 market access written into the text, threatening ratification opposition if excluded
Supply_chain_mfr raised unresolved concern about sunset clause creating investment uncertainty despite locked enforcement framework
key_conflicts: Canada refused 75% day-one RVC without concessions on dairy/Chapter 19; threatened to walk
Dairy_ag demanded written market access vs. USTR's refusal to put dairy schedule in text
Labor_union vs. auto_industry on enforcement teeth: tariff suspension vs. remediation windows
Congress declared dairy and Chapter 19 'off the table' for labor enforcement trades
key_concessions: USTR offered 65-70-75% RVC glide path instead of day-one 75% (major shift to accommodate Canada and supply chains)
Canada accepted 75% final RVC in exchange for glide path, ministerial statement, and locked enforcement
Dairy_ag accepted ministerial statement in ratification instrument instead of written market access schedule
Mexico accepted trilateral audit panel with escalation authority despite sovereignty concerns
red_lines: Canada: Chapter 19 dispute settlement and dairy supply management preservation (resolved via ministerial statement)
USTR: no written dairy concessions in main text; bilateral-with-Mexico threat if Canada blocked
Labor_union: enforceable wage-floor audits with real tariff consequences, not aspirational language
Congress: labor enforcement must be auditable with penalties to secure ratification votes
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Sunset clause investment uncertainty raised by supply_chain_mfr in final round but never resolved or addressed by USTR/Congress
Repeat-violation escalation mechanism for labor audits questioned by labor_union but not definitively answered before filing
Dairy_ag's ratification support conditioned on legally binding ministerial language, but enforceability mechanism not detailed
downstream_risk_variables: Sunset clause remains unresolved—could freeze long-term Mexican plant investment despite locked labor enforcement
Trilateral panel's repeat-violation escalation authority unclear—may undermine labor enforcement credibility
Ministerial statement's legal enforceability in ratification instrument untested—could face congressional challenge
Quarterly audit operational capacity and trilateral coordination not stress-tested
Dairy_ag board approval still pending despite leader's commitment
uncertainty_notes: Sunset clause review mechanism never addressed despite supply_chain_mfr raising it as critical to investment decisions. Repeat-violation escalation rule for labor audits questioned but not confirmed in operational protocol before filing. Dairy_ag's board approval assumed but not secured. Ministerial statement's binding legal status in ratification instrument asserted by USTR but mechanism not detailed.

marker_evidence.auto_rules_bottleneck: 75% RVC was the central blocking issue R1-R2; Canada's refusal drove the glide-path compromise that unlocked the entire package
marker_evidence.labor_enforcement_key: Auditable $16/hour wage floor with tariff suspension was Congress's stated ratification condition; drove operational protocol design and filing
marker_evidence.canada_dairy_final_issue: Dairy raised repeatedly by Canada and dairy_ag as needed concession, but resolved via ministerial statement without blocking—acknowledged but not decisive
marker_evidence.dispute_settlement_canada_redline: Chapter 19 preservation demanded by Canada as cabinet requirement, but resolved via same ministerial statement as dairy—raised but not blocking
marker_evidence.sunset_to_review_compromise: Mentioned only once by supply_chain_mfr in R5 as unresolved concern; no discussion, no proposal, no response—single passing mention
marker_evidence.ratification_risk: Congress's ratification support was the explicit forcing mechanism in R4-R5 that compelled dairy_ag to accept and USTR to file; shaped final package structure
marker_evidence.supply_chain_adjustment: Auto_industry and supply_chain_mfr raised compliance costs and sourcing freezes as concerns driving glide-path need, but did not block or redirect—acknowledged consideration
marker_evidence.us_mexico_first_pressures_canada: USTR's bilateral-deal threat in R1-R2 was explicit leverage forcing Canada to accept glide path and move on dairy/Ch19; drove Canada's concession
